facts.text: Richwood began as a wooded tract settled in the late 19th century by sharecroppers who cleared land and built a rudimentary school that became the town’s early hub.
The town officially incorporated on December 31, 1974, under Louisiana Revised Statute 33:52.
Richwood’s climate is humid subtropical, with hot, humid summers and mild, wet winters influenced by Gulf of Mexico moisture.
In 1940, a donation of two acres by Napoleon Brown Sr. enabled the first dedicated school building, formalizing Richwood’s educational infrastructure.
After incorporation, Richwood evolved from a rural enclave into a suburban community, largely residential, adjacent to Monroe.
The town hosts a privately operated correctional center, a notable institution that has drawn attention for its operational challenges.
